Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Middleton and the surrounding Midlothian region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional bathroom installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Midlothian, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any full bathroom installation and fitting requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Middleton with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: Can you move the toilet and bath to different positions?
faqs.a: Yes, but it depends on the soil pipe route and floor structure. Moving a toilet more than a metre from the existing soil stack requires a new soil pipe connection and increases cost significantly.

faqs.q: How much does a bathroom installation cost?
faqs.a: Suite and tile costs are separate.

faqs.q: Should I supply my own bathroom suite or let the plumber supply it?
faqs.a: You can do either. Supplying your own suite gives you more choice and control over the brand and style. Your installer may offer trade discounts worth 15-30% off RRP if they supply.

faqs.q: What guarantees should I expect on a bathroom installation?
faqs.a: Expect a minimum 12-month labour guarantee. Manufacturer warranties on suites and fittings typically run 5-25 years depending on the brand. Get all guarantees in writing.

localParagraph: Middleton, a rural village in Midlothian, Scotland, sits within a landscape of mixed housing that ranges from traditional stone farmhouses and period cottages to more modern rural conversions, each presenting its own set of challenges for bathroom installation work. The area's mixed water hardness means that local plumbers and bathroom fitters need to account for the potential for both scale build-up and corrosion when selecting pipework, fixtures, and fittings — a consideration that can significantly affect the longevity of any new bathroom installation. Older properties in and around Middleton often feature original plumbing systems that require careful assessment before any new suite is fitted, while newer builds may demand a different approach to achieving the right water pressure and flow rates. Homeowners in this part of Midlothian benefit from working with experienced bathroom installers who understand how Scotland's variable water conditions and the region's diverse property stock interact, ensuring that every installation is planned with both the building's character and long-term practicality firmly in mind.
whatItInvolves: A full bathroom installation covers everything from stripping out the existing suite to fitting the new one — including all pipework, waste connections, tiling preparation, flooring, and electrical work for lighting and extraction. A quality bathroom installation transforms one of the most-used rooms in your home and typically adds 3-5% to your property value.
process: The process starts with a detailed survey to assess existing pipework, drainage routes, and structural considerations. Day 1-2: strip out and prep. Day 3-4: first fix plumbing and any structural work. Day 5-7: suite installation, tiling, and second fix. Day 8-10: finishing, sealant, and final inspection. You'll be without a working bathroom for 5-10 days depending on complexity — we'll agree a realistic timeline upfront.
whatToExpect: Expect a detailed written quote covering labour, waste disposal, and any structural work. Suite and tiles are usually supplied separately by you or sourced through us. All plumbing work is carried out to Water Regulations standards. A bathroom installation is a major investment — ask to see previous work and Gas Safe registration before committing to any installer.
intro: A full bathroom installation is one of the highest-value home improvements you can make in the UK, typically adding 3-5% to your property value. The project covers everything from stripping out your existing bathroom to fitting a completely new suite — including all plumbing, tiling, waterproofing, electrics, and finishing work. Whether you are upgrading a tired 1990s bathroom, converting a spare bedroom into an en-suite, or building a wet room for accessibility, the quality of the installer makes the difference between a bathroom that lasts 20 years and one that causes problems within 5. A typical full bathroom installation takes 5-10 working days from strip-out to completion, though more complex projects involving structural changes or bespoke designs can take up to three weeks.
serviceDetail: A professional bathroom installation follows a structured sequence. The work begins with a detailed survey — your installer will assess existing pipework routing, waste positions, soil stack location, and electrical capacity. This determines what is straightforward and what will need modification. Strip-out and preparation typically takes 1-2 days, including removing the old suite, tiles, and any damaged plasterwork. First-fix plumbing follows — this is where new hot and cold supply pipes, waste runs, and any soil pipe modifications are installed before the walls are closed up. Plastering and tanking (waterproofing) come next, which is critical for showers and wet rooms. Tiling is usually the longest single phase, followed by second-fix plumbing where the bath, basin, WC, and shower are connected. Electrical work — extractor fans, heated towel rails, spot lighting — is coordinated alongside. The final stage is silicone sealing, accessory fitting, and a thorough clean and test of all installations.
pricing: Labour costs for a full bathroom installation in the UK typically range from £2,500 to £5,500 depending on the size of the room, complexity of the design, and regional labour rates. A complete renovation including all materials — suite, tiles, waterproofing, and finishing — usually comes in between £4,000 and £12,000 for a standard family bathroom. En-suite installations tend to cost less (£3,000-£7,000) due to the smaller footprint, while luxury bathrooms with underfloor heating, walk-in showers, and bespoke tiling can exceed £15,000. The biggest cost variables are the suite itself (£300 for budget to £3,000+ for premium brands), tiling (£20-£80 per square metre installed), and any structural modifications needed. Always get a fixed written quote that breaks down labour, materials, waste disposal, and any provisional sums.
whyLocal: Bathroom installation is one of the most location-sensitive plumbing jobs. A local installer understands the specific property types in your area — whether that means navigating the narrow stud walls and limited soil pipe access of a Victorian terrace, working with the concrete floors common in 1960s council housing, or dealing with the lightweight partition walls in modern new-builds. Local knowledge also matters for practical reasons: understanding which merchants stock the right materials nearby, knowing local building control requirements for electrical work in bathrooms, and being available for the inevitable follow-up visit if a tap develops a slow drip three weeks after installation. An installer based within 30 minutes of your home will also keep costs lower — no inflated travel charges, no delayed starts, and realistic scheduling because they know the area.
